content.en: The **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** is a quantitative index that tracks the growth rates in different industry groups of the economy. It is compiled and published monthly by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. It serves as a barometer for industrial activity in the Indian economy.
content.hi: The **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** is a quantitative index that tracks the growth rates in different industry groups of the economy. It is compiled and published monthly by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. It serves as a barometer for industrial activity in the Indian economy.

definition.en: Different industries are assigned weights based on their relative importance in the industrial sector.
definition.hi: Different industries are assigned weights based on their relative importance in the industrial sector.

content.en: The eight core industries (Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity) carry a significant weight in the IIP.
content.hi: The eight core industries (Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity) carry a significant weight in the IIP.

content.en: Students often confuse IIP with GDP growth; remember that IIP is a volume-based index, not a value-based one.
content.hi: Students often confuse IIP with GDP growth; remember that IIP is a volume-based index, not a value-based one.

content.en: Focus on the weightage of the eight core industries as they are frequently asked in Prelims.
